A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BTL-UI research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison, including the checklist added in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original BTL-UI results on ScreenSpot, ScreenSpot-V2, ScreenSpot-Pro, AndroidControl and GUI-Odyssey, together with ablations and a trajectory case study.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark results, ablations and the trajectory case study, while revising some scores and expanding baseline comparisons.

M1.justification: The Blink-Think-Link procedure, two-stage ROI annotation pipeline, three reward components, GRPO optimization and Qwen2.5-VL backbones remain unchanged. The expanded Hungarian-matching explanation and corrected prompt-tag typography do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Evaluation coverage is unchanged: ScreenSpot-Pro moves from v1 Appendix A into v3's main text. However, Table 1 replaces one of v1's two ShowUI-Desktop training rows with ShowUI-Web. The PDFs do not establish whether this corrects a duplicated label or represents an actual change in training-domain coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds UI-TARS-2B/7B to all grounding and planning comparisons, UGround-V1-2B/7B to ScreenSpot, and OS-Atlas-Pro-4B/7B to planning. These evaluated comparators substantially strengthen the comparison set; UI-TARS exceeds BTL-UI on the reported overall grounding accuracies and planning success rates.

E3.justification: The reported BTL-UI model sizes, training sample counts, high- versus low-level inputs, action space, evaluation metrics and selected ROI count remain unchanged. Added Avg caption explanations do not establish a changed aggregation procedure. No revised testing protocol is specified for the changed scores.

E4.justification: v1 Table 5 and v3 Table 6 contain the same training-component ablations and ROI-count sensitivity analysis. The AndroidControl trajectory, including its annotation-error example, is also retained. No new robustness tests, failure analyses or case studies appear.

E5.justification: v1 Appendix D and v3 Appendix C identically specify seed 2025 for data sampling and training. Neither provides repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new checklist claims quantitative error metrics are supplied, but none are presented in the supplied PDF.

E6.justification: Between v1 Table 4 and v3 Table 5, reported GUI-Odyssey SR changes from 43.2 to 64.0 for BTL-UI-3B and 45.2 to 65.4 for 7B; Type and GR also change. These unexplained revisions are not demonstrated same-setting gains. SeeClick's ScreenSpot-V2 average changes from 53.4 to 55.1, and BTL-UI-7B's ScreenSpot-Pro Creative/Text score changes from 54.4 to 26.7 while its average remains 33.7. Added baseline results also change overall rankings. The stated ablation gain changes from 3.8 to 3.6 points despite unchanged table values.

T1.justification: The formal interaction description, ROI selection, reward definitions, advantage calculation and optimization objective in Equations 1–9 are mathematically unchanged. Added element subscripts, multiplication notation and matching explanations introduce no new assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and third contribution replace the broad claim of state-of-the-art performance across GUI benchmarks with competitive performance. This materially narrows the headline empirical contribution, consistent with the stronger baselines. The cognitive-framework, annotation-pipeline and process-outcome reward novelty claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 now acknowledges overall grounding and planning gaps to UI-TARS and emphasizes mobile-subtask strengths and competitiveness with less training data. Planning gains are interpreted through Blink/Link synergy and reduced accumulated errors. The output-length overhead limitation and annotation-noise case interpretation remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 clarifies Avg in grounding-table captions and adds checklist promises to release code, checkpoints and reproduction instructions upon acceptance; actual availability is not established. Conversely, v1's explicit H100-80G hardware description disappears from the experimental setup, with only H100 mentioned in the checklist. No substantive training hyperparameters are newly supplied.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 41 works, and the related-work sections retain their substantive coverage. v3 nevertheless refines its positioning relative to UI-TARS and OS-Atlas, explicitly discussing UI-TARS' reported 50B-token training and presenting BTL-UI as a competitive alternative requiring less training data.

P1.justification: v3 makes distributed language and terminology corrections, expands the matching explanation, merges the low- and high-level planning discussions, and integrates ScreenSpot-Pro into the main results narrative. It reorganizes the corresponding appendices and appends a NeurIPS checklist, while preserving the main scientific section structure.

P2.justification: Result tables gain baseline rows, revised ordering and updated best-result emphasis; grounding captions explain Avg. ScreenSpot-Pro moves from appendix Table 6 to main-text Table 4. The four figures retain their content, with the trajectory figure relocated, and prompt typography and surrounding page layout receive limited adjustments.

improvement.justification: The stronger baseline comparisons and retreat from blanket state-of-the-art claims make v3's empirical positioning more credible. These are useful but limited gains: substantial GUI-Odyssey score revisions remain unexplained, the revised ablation-gain prose conflicts with the unchanged table, and the new checklist claims uncertainty reporting that is absent. The revision improves comparison and claim calibration without substantially improving methodological validation or reproducibility.
